content:
#1 Hi all,

I maintain an open-source community project called PhysLean (https://github.com/HEPLean/PhysLean) which aims to formalize results from physics into the interactive theorem prover Lean 4. I was wondering if it might be appropriate to create an nLab page for the project — I’d be happy to put in the work? No problem at all if you think it’s not a good fit.

Before moving into computer science, I worked on infinty-topos theory and functorial field theory applied to symmetries in physics, so I made heavy use of the nLab. I’m really grateful for all the work that goes into it — thank you!

Best wishes,
Joseph Tooby-Smith.
subject: PhysLean

content:
#3 Does github:PhysLean use any category theory? I don’t mean just categories and functors but showing things like adjunctions are fundamentally involved.

I’ve been skim following PhysLean progress on Bluesky:physlean.
subject: PhysLean

content:
#4 Hey, it's got some category theory in the set-up of index notation, but this is just categories and functors unfortunately. Nothing using adjunctions.
At somepoint I would like for it to include TQFTs, and some of the recent work on category theory in generalized symmetries, but I personally haven't had the time to do this yet. We're also slowed a bit by what is in Mathlib, for example,I think currently it would be quite hard to define the cobordism category in any dimension (even the unextended versions).
